approaches.name: core banking, supervision and registry IT modernization
approaches.description: The project upgrades DAB's core banking and supervision systems, collateral and credit registries, and deposit insurance payout software to strengthen oversight and financial intermediation. Practices: New core banking system and automated banking supervision at DAB; IT modernization of collateral registry and public credit registry; MIS for insured deposit payout operations; Core banking system modernization for central bank oversight; IT modernization of collateral and public credit registries; Single Customer View depositor data and payout software for deposit insurance; credit registry expansion to utility and telecom payment data.
approaches.why_innovative: New system: CBS plus automated supervision replacing manual oversight | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: Specifically, DAB plans to install a new core banking system (CBS),and automate relevant aspects of banking supervision, thus strengthening its overall operational and oversight capacity.

extra_evidence.text: Further measures aimed at strengthening banking system oversight include upgrades in DAB’s IT infrastructure and capacity building of DAB’s technical directorates.
DAB has established a collateral registry (CR) for movable property in 2013 followed by public credit registry (PCR) in 2014 and both systems are due for information technology (IT) upgrade.

6 The World Bank Strengthening Afghanistan’s Financial Intermediation (P171886) enables lenders to effectively use borrowers’ movable property as collateral, and credit information provided by the PCR is a primary factor in evaluating the creditworthiness of banks clients and mitigating credit risk; thus, both registries are essential for facilitating access to finance.
The required investment in Management Information System (MIS) - hardware and software for insured deposits’ payout - will be financed from Component 4: Enhancing DAB’s IT Infrastructure.

Capital injection of US$15 million is expected to be disbursed to the DIF in two rounds governed with formal disbursement conditions: i) first disbursement upon enactment of the law on deposit insurance (expected within 2 years from project effectiveness); and ii) second disbursement upon development of MIS and payout procedures (as required under the law).

Representative project activities include: i) modernization of the Core Banking System to strengthen DAB's oversight and risk management capacity; ii) automation of relevant aspects of banking supervision; iii) investment in critical IT to operationalize deposit insurance function (i.e. management information systems, hardware and software); and iv) IT modernization of the collateral registry and public credit registry to facilitate financial intermediation.

A set of secondary regulation will therefore need to be developed to support DIS’ payout function including but not limited to those regulating insured deposits payout through Single Customer View (SCV) data on depositors and development of a tailor- made software in support of compensation process.

In order to improve DIS authority’s ability to compensate depositors in compliance with international standards the following activities are recommended: i) DIS authority and DAB to sign Memorandum of Understanding regulating flow of information; ii) DIS authority to approve regulation on insured deposits compensation; and iii) DIS authority to develop MIS in support for deposit payout.

To further develop and provide a comprehensive credit information services, the PCR department plans to extend PCR with development of additional data structures coverage to non-regulated entities in the utilities and telecoms sector thus expanding the information database and outreach to customers without credit history and facilitating their access to finance.
